## The case

You are the data analyst on a small study. Your client is the channel manager at a small creator
agency that represents about a dozen Twitch streamers. The agency is about to pitch a sponsor on
how engaged its streamers' chats are. Before the pitch, the manager wants three questions
answered with data:

1. Does chat in gaming channels look different from chat in non-gaming channels?
2. Does a bigger audience change how people write?
3. How much of chat is reaction (an emote, a cheer, a single word) and how much is commentary?

**Where the job stands.** In Data Wrangling you built the table, `data/twitch_analysis.RDS`,
with your thirty hand-coded messages inside it. The manager has not seen a number from it yet.

**Your job.** Show the manager what is in the table before anything is tested: how often each
category occurs, how long messages run, how two categories line up, and what the patterns look
like in a chart. The manager does not read R, so every **Write:** prompt is a note to them.

## Your assignment

| Part | What you do | Why the client needs it |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Frequency tables: count how often each category occurs | The manager sees how much of chat is gaming, large-audience, and reaction |
| 2 | The three numbers: the mean, median, and standard deviation of message length | "How people write" becomes numbers the manager can compare |
| 3 | The cross-tabulation: count viewer band against channel type | The manager sees whether audience size and channel type go together |
| 4 | Three figures, each with alt text, a disclosure sentence, and an interpretation | A chart is what the manager can put in front of a sponsor |
| Last | Explain this stage to the client, in one short paragraph | The manager gets what you found in plain language |

The code sits in gray boxes called chunks, as in Data Wrangling. Work through them in order:

1. Replace each blank, shown as `___`, with the code it needs.
2. Click **Run Cell** at the top left of the gray box.
3. Compare what R prints with **What you should see**.

Where the worksheet says **Write:**, type your answer in your own words. Every task has a
**Help** link. It opens the page that explains that task: what the blank needs, where to click,
and what to do when R prints an error.

## Setup

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(tidyverse)     # tables and charts
library(v2v)           # theme_v2v() and the course palette
options(scipen = 10)  # long numbers such as timestamps print in full; p-values keep the usual form

analysis <- read_rds("data/twitch_analysis.RDS")  # the table worksheet 1 saved
dir.create("figures", showWarnings = FALSE)        # where every chart is saved

analysis %>%
  count(reaction_only)  # your hand-coded variable made it through
```

**What you should see:** your two coded groups adding to `30`, and `NA` with `35237`.
[Help with Setup](https://aura-lab.siue.edu/v2v-hub/resources/help/describing-data.html#setup)

## Part 1: Frequency tables

### Task 1.1: Channel type

A frequency table says how often each category occurs. This one is done for you as the model.

```{r}
#| label: freq-channel-type
analysis %>%
  count(channel_type) %>%                  # messages per category
  mutate(percent = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1))  # and as a share of all messages
```

**What you should see:** `gaming` `31309` (88.8%), `non-gaming` `3457` (9.8%), and `NA` `501`
(1.4%).
[Help with Task 1.1](https://aura-lab.siue.edu/v2v-hub/resources/help/describing-data.html#task-1-1)

### Task 1.2: Viewer band

Build the same table for `viewer_band`.

```{r}
#| label: freq-viewer-band
analysis %>%
  ___(___) %>%
  mutate(percent = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1))
```

**What you should see:** `small` `27766` (78.7%), `medium` `5501` (15.6%), `large` `2000` (5.7%).
[Help with Task 1.2](https://aura-lab.siue.edu/v2v-hub/resources/help/describing-data.html#task-1-2)

### Task 1.3: Your hand-coded variable

Only thirty messages carry a code. Keep those rows first, or the table is mostly `NA`.

```{r}
#| label: freq-reaction
analysis %>%
  filter(!is.na(___)) %>%  # only the thirty coded messages
  count(reaction_only) %>%
  mutate(percent = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1))
```

**What you should see:** two rows adding to `30`.
[Help with Task 1.3](https://aura-lab.siue.edu/v2v-hub/resources/help/describing-data.html#task-1-3)

**Write:** two to three sentences for the client on the three tables: what they show, and what
they do not. Name the numbers.

## Part 2: The three numbers

### Task 2.1: Message length, all messages

```{r}
#| label: length-all
analysis %>%
  summarize(
    n      = sum(!is.na(message_length)),
    mean   = mean(message_length, na.rm = TRUE),
    median = median(message_length, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd     = sd(message_length, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
```

**What you should see:** `n` `35263`, `mean` `29.0`, `median` `17`, `sd` `41.2`.
[Help with Task 2.1](https://aura-lab.siue.edu/v2v-hub/resources/help/describing-data.html#task-2-1)

### Task 2.2: By channel type, and by your code

Fill the grouping variable, then the filter that keeps only your coded messages.

```{r}

  filter(!is.na(channel_type)) %>%
  ___(___) %>%

    n      = n(),
    mean   = mean(message_length, na.rm = TRUE),
    median = median(message_length, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd     = sd(message_length, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

analysis %>%
  filter(!is.na(___)) %>%
  group_by(___) %>%
  summarize(
    n      = n(),
    mean   = mean(message_length),
    median = median(message_length),
    sd     = sd(message_length),
    max    = max(message_length)
  )
```

**What you should see:** `gaming` n `31309`, mean `28.5`, median `17`, sd `38.5`; `non-gaming`
n `3457`, mean `33.7`, median `16`, sd `60.7`. Then one row for each of your two coded groups.
[Help with Task 2.2](https://aura-lab.siue.edu/v2v-hub/resources/help/describing-data.html#task-2-2)

## Part 3: The cross-tabulation

### Task 3.1: Viewer band by channel type

```{r}
#| label: crosstab
analysis %>%
  filter(!is.na(channel_type)) %>%
  count(___, ___) %>%                   # viewer band as the rows, channel type as the columns
  pivot_wider(names_from = ___, values_from = n, values_fill = 0)   # one column per channel type
```

**What you should see:** three rows of counts. `small`: `25309` gaming, `2457` non-gaming.
`medium`: `4000` and `1000`. `large`: `2000` and `0`.
[Help with Task 3.1](https://aura-lab.siue.edu/v2v-hub/resources/help/describing-data.html#task-3-1)

### Task 3.2: As proportions of each band

The same counts as shares of each band.

```{r}
#| label: crosstab-shares
analysis %>%
  filter(!is.na(channel_type)) %>%
  count(viewer_band, channel_type) %>%
  ___(viewer_band) %>%                           # shares within each band, not across the table
  mutate(share = round(n / sum(n), 3))
```

**What you should see:** non-gaming is `0.088` of the small band and `0.2` of the medium band.
The large band has no non-gaming row.
[Help with Task 3.2](https://aura-lab.siue.edu/v2v-hub/resources/help/describing-data.html#task-3-2)

**Write:** two to three sentences for the client on the cross-tabulation. What does it show, and
what can it not show yet?

## Part 4: Figures

Each figure is built, saved to `figures/` by the code that makes it, and carries alt text you
write on its `#| fig-alt:` line. After each one, **Write:** one sentence disclosing a choice you
made in it (a cap on an axis, which categories you kept, a bin width), and two to three
sentences of interpretation for the client.

### Task 4.1: Channel type within each viewer band

A proportion bar chart of the cross-tabulation. Fill the fill aesthetic and the position that
makes every bar the same height.

```{r}
#| label: fig-band-type
#| fig-alt: "YOUR TURN: one sentence saying what this chart shows."
fig_band_type <- analysis %>%
  filter(!is.na(channel_type)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = viewer_band, fill = ___)) +
  geom_bar(position = "___") +                        # every bar scaled to 100%
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format()) +
  scale_fill_v2v() +
  labs(title   = "Channel type within each viewer band",
       x       = "Viewer band (channel's median viewers)",
       y       = "Share of messages",
       fill    = "Channel type",
       caption = "Source: v2v Twitch corpus, November 18 to 24, 2018. 501 messages with no channel type left out.") +
  theme_v2v()

fig_band_type
ggsave("figures/band-by-type.png", fig_band_type, width = 7, height = 4.5, dpi = 300)
```

**What you should see:** three bars of equal height, and `band-by-type.png` in `figures/`.
[Help with Task 4.1](https://aura-lab.siue.edu/v2v-hub/resources/help/describing-data.html#task-4-1)

**Write:** the disclosure sentence, then two to three sentences of interpretation.

*Your answer:*

### Task 4.2: Message length by your code

The thirty coded messages, as a boxplot. Fill the variable on the x axis and the geom.

```{r}
#| label: fig-length-reaction
#| fig-alt: "YOUR TURN: one sentence saying what this chart shows."
fig_length_reaction <- analysis %>%
  filter(!is.na(reaction_only)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = ___, y = message_length)) +
  ___(outlier.shape = NA) +   # no outlier dots here; the points below show every message
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, alpha = 0.6) +   # every one of the thirty, shown as a point
  labs(title   = "Message length by message type",
       x       = "Hand-coded message type",
       y       = "Characters",
       caption = "Source: 30 hand-coded messages, 15 each from bobross and giantwaffle.") +
  theme_v2v()

fig_length_reaction
ggsave("figures/length-by-reaction.png", fig_length_reaction, width = 6, height = 4.5, dpi = 300)
```

**What you should see:** two boxes, and `length-by-reaction.png` in `figures/`.
[Help with Task 4.2](https://aura-lab.siue.edu/v2v-hub/resources/help/describing-data.html#task-4-2)

**Write:** the disclosure sentence, then two to three sentences of interpretation.
